actions.action: Remove the plant from its pot and wash all old soil off the roots
Soak the bare roots for about 30 minutes in water with 3% hydrogen peroxide (1 tsp per 1.5 L)
Keep the plant in a container of plain water for about a month to regrow roots
Cut off the top part and try rooting it in water
Repot into a new pot with peat-based universal soil and perlite, optionally with expanded clay at the bottom, keeping the stem base shallow
Give the first watering with hydrogen peroxide solution (1 tsp per liter)
Check the topsoil with a finger and water only when the top layer is dry

verdict.reason: The answer explicitly gives no diagnosis. Its soak in water partly overlaps the fix, but it is buried in drastic steps. Bare-rooting and month-long water culture of a merely dry plant risks root stress and rot.
